title_en: Comic Book 'Journey to the West 29: Biqiu Kingdom'
source_file: 连环画《西游记29：比丘国》（6-10岁）.pdf
full_text_zh:
[P1] 比丘国
《西游记》之二十九
原著 吴承恩
改编 陈平夫
绘画 轩辕观潮
河北美术出版社

[P2] 内容提要
这本连环画是根据古典神话小说《西游记》中第七十八——七十九回编绘的。描写唐僧师徒四人去西天取经路过比丘国，发现国王被妖魔所缠，身染重病。昏庸的国王听信妖言，要用一千多个男孩的心肝做药引。为此传下圣旨，命百姓选送小儿，装入鹅笼，听候使用。为了搭救孩童，孙悟空深入王宫，识破“国丈”和国王宠爱的“美后”是白鹿和白面狐精变化，于是施展神威，降伏白鹿，打死狐精。二妖现了原形，国王羞惭难当，低头认错。一千多个小孩的性命得救了，全城百姓感恩戴德，塑下唐僧师徒的影像，永远纪念他们的恩情。
1 西天路上，有一个比丘国，国王昏庸无道。一天早朝，忽然来了一位道人，要把自己的女儿献给国王。国王一见倾心，便选上金殿封为美后，那道人也被封为国丈。

[P3] 2 国王自从有了美后，昼夜贪欢，不理朝政。不到三年工夫，弄得面黄肌瘦，百病缠身，经太医院调治无效，眼看性命难保。
3 这时国丈进宫奏道：‘我有海外秘方，百药齐备，只差一千一百一十一个男孩心肝作药引，国王若能取来心肝，配药煎服，不惟起死回生，还能千年不老。’

[P4] 4 昏王一听大喜，当即传旨按户选送，命令先把小儿装入鹅笼，放在各户门前听候使用。
5 这时，唐僧师徒四人，正由此城经过，看见家家门前放着一个鹅笼，甚觉奇怪。

[P5] 6 悟空立刻变个蜜蜂，飞进鹅笼一看，原来里面装的
全是五六岁的小男孩，有的在玩，有的在哭。悟空更觉事情蹊跷。
7 看看日落西山，四人便赶到金亭馆驿（官员招待所）
投宿，驿丞（管馆驿的官）听说他们是东土大唐来的和尚，
格外客气，马上让进上房。

[P6] 8 吃罢晚饭，唐僧打听起鹅笼的事儿来，把驿丞吓了一跳，急忙过来低声说：‘长老，这事不必过问，你明天换了关文，只管赶路好了。’
9 唐僧觉得其中必有缘故，扯住驿丞，定要问个明白。驿丞无奈，只得叫佣人走开，把鹅笼的事情讲了一遍，讲完就溜走了。

[P7] 10 唐僧听了，不禁一阵心酸，忙同三位徒弟商量搭救众小儿性命的办法。八戒说：‘只管宽衣睡觉，莫替别人担忧。’唐僧骂道：‘你这个不慈悯的东西，人命关天，怎能不管呢！’
11 沙僧说：‘师父不要悲伤，等明天倒换关文时，问明白后再作道理。’悟空道：‘师弟说得有理，师父放心，那国丈若是个妖怪，俺一定用金箍棒拿他，断不能叫他伤害小儿们的性命。’

[P8] 12 唐僧想了想说：‘我们若问此事，那昏王不分远近，全把我们当作造谣的人问罪如何是好？’悟空附耳道：‘如此，如此……’唐僧连称：‘妙极！快去。’
13 悟空一个跟斗起在空中，念动真言，本地城皇、土地马上一齐来到跟前，听候吩咐。

[P9] 14 悟空道：‘烦请诸位，把鹅笼移到城外收藏起来，好好喂养小儿，不得惊吓，等我除了妖邪，再来还我。’众神听令，只见一阵狂风，鹅笼全不见了。
15 次日，唐僧换好衣服去见国王。悟空放心不下，变了个小虫儿，叮在师父的帽沿上，暗地保护。

[P10] 16 国王一听是东土大唐来的取经和尚，心想：‘远来之僧，必有道行。’于是强打精神，由内侍搀扶着上殿接见。
17 唐僧上殿朝拜，换罢关文，刚刚坐定，就听当驾官上前奏道：‘国丈爷爷来了。’

[P11] 18 国丈在金殿坐定后，唐僧上前施礼，他却昂然不睬。
19 国丈问道：‘僧家何来？’国王道：‘是东土大唐差往西天取经的，到此倒换关文。’国丈笑道：‘自来和尚全是瞎修瞎炼，俗话说：“坐、坐、坐，坐得屁股破……”’说得满朝文武，哄堂大笑。

[P12] 20 唐僧和他争辩了几句，怎奈那国丈凶焰万丈。再加国王随声附和，百官跟着帮腔，弄得唐僧十分无趣，便辞下金殿。这时，只听悟空叫道：‘这国丈是妖精。你先回去，我在这里听听消息。’
21 唐僧走后，悟空飞进金殿，刚刚叮在翡翠屏上，只见卫兵报道：‘启禀国王，大事不好。昨夜一阵怪风，把全城的鹅笼刮得无影无踪。’国王大惊，连连顿足道：‘我没有小儿的心肝治病，活不成了。’

[P13] 22 国丈对国王说：‘如果吃了和尚的心肝，比小儿的还好。’昏王一听，转忧为喜，埋怨道：‘国丈何不早说，刚才不放那和尚走掉多好。’国丈道：‘这有何难，传旨围住馆驿，哪怕他飞上天去！’
23 悟空听得明明白白，急忙飞回馆驿，报与师父知道。唐僧一听，吓得目瞪口呆，一把扯住悟空哀求道：‘贤徒救我！’悟空道：‘若要好，大做小，师变徒，徒变师，我替你前去。’

[P14] 24 说变就变，悟空用泥按着自己的脸形，做好模子，往师父脸上一贴，吹口气，唐僧马上变成了悟空。
25 悟空又和师父换了衣服，自己把身子一摇，变作唐僧，弄得八戒和沙僧都认不出来了。

[P15] 26 顷刻间，只听一声喧嚷，拥进无数官兵，为首的一个官员要见唐僧。悟空假装施礼道：‘贫僧便是。’那官员并不答话，拉着悟空就走。
27 推推拥拥，把悟空拉上金殿，悟空挺立阶前高声叫道：‘比丘王，请贫僧到来，有话快讲吧！’

[P16] 快拿刀来，剖开胸膛，若有黑心，一定送你。
要你那颗黑心。
28 国王道：“我患重病，药味全备，只差药引。长老若肯将心肝送与我作了药引，我给你修建祠堂，四时祭祀。”
悟空一阵冷笑道：“贫僧的心倒有几个，但不知国王要什么颜色的？”
29 悟空剖开肚皮，只见咕噜噜滚出一堆心来，红的，黄的，白的……就是没有黑的。吓得百官抱头闭目，国王全身如筛糠，直叫：“快收了去，快收了去。”

[P17] 30 悟空一抹脸，现出本相说道：‘我们和尚家都是一片好心，惟有你这国丈才有可作药引的黑心，待我剜来你用。’
31 国丈一看，认出是当年的齐天大圣到了，抽身就跑。悟空举棒就打，那国丈急用蟠龙杖来迎。一来一往，打了二十多个回合，不分胜负。

[P18] 32 悟空越战越勇，国丈哪是他的对手，眼看招架不住，
便虚幌一拐，化作一道寒光溜走了。
33 悟空按落云头，到了殿下，满朝文武一齐过来拜见。
悟空道：‘莫拜了，快去找找你们的国王吧！’

[P19] 34 大家分头去找，先到美后宫，没有找到，连美后也不见了。
35 正在忙乱，只见四五个太监搀着半死不活的昏王，从后殿走了出来。

[P20] 36 百官上前接驾，齐声奏道：‘幸遇神僧到此，辨明国丈是个妖邪。宫内不见美后，想是一同逃走了。’
37 国王睁开眼，愣了半天，才扶着悟空问道：‘我早间见过你一次，如今你怎么变了样子呢？’悟空道：‘我是他的徒弟孙悟空，因为你要吃我师父的心肝，我才变作他的模样前来降妖。’

[P21] 38 国王听罢浑身打战，如捣蒜般地叩头，乞求悟空饶恕。又急忙整衣冠，传旨请唐僧上殿。
39 唐僧领着八戒、沙僧，到了殿下。悟空迎上前去，把师父的泥脸抓下，换好衣服，叫声“变”，只见唐僧又还了原形。

[P22] 40 国王一见唐僧到了，马上下位迎接，口称：‘法师老佛’，搀扶上殿。
41 大家坐定，悟空问道：‘国王的岳丈和美后来自何方？待俺一并拿来，剪除后患。’羞得国王满脸通红，道：‘他们来时，说是住在城南七十里柳林坡清华庄上。’

[P23] 42 悟空听罢，当即吩咐沙僧好好保护师父，同八戒驾起风云，寻找清华庄捉妖去了。
43 二人飞行七十里，住下风云，但见杨柳深处，夹着一条小河，一望无际，怎么也找不到村庄。

[P24] 44 悟空念咒找来土地问路，土地道：“此处有一清华洞，内藏妖邪，大圣要找，由此向前，见了九叉头老杨树，左转三转，右转三转，用手猛拍，连叫三声开门，那清华洞就出现了。”
45 二人照着方向找去，果然找到一棵九叉头老杨树。悟空命八戒站开等候接应，自己照话行事，只听一声巨响，闪开两扇洞门，石屏上写着四个大字：“清华洞府”。

[P25] 46 悟空闯进洞去，只见那老妖怀里搂了个美女，喘吁吁地说：‘好事不成，眼看小儿的心肝吃到嘴里，却被那个该死的孙悟空给搅坏了。’
47 悟空一个箭步跳到老妖跟前，喝道：‘害人的妖邪吃我一棒。’吓得老妖魂飞天外，丢开美女就跑。

[P26] 48 八戒在洞外等得心烦，正要进洞看看动静，恰遇老妖跑了出来，他便迎头一钯筑去，那老妖急忙闪开，将身一晃，化道寒光往东逃走。
49 二人紧紧追赶，追着追着老妖不见了。云端闪出南极仙翁。八戒问道：‘肉头老儿，你见妖邪没有？’原来那妖缩成一团躲在寿星身后。寿星指着那妖道：‘在这里，在这里。’

[P27] 50 悟空道：‘寿星老弟，那老妖作怪害人，你怎么袒护它！’寿星陪礼道：‘大圣息怒，它是我的脚力——白鹿。是我不慎，被它盗走拐杖，偷跑出来作怪，还望大圣饶恕！’
51 悟空思忖了一会道：‘幸亏比丘国小儿没有被害，不然，绝不饶恕它！’吓得老妖浑身打战。寿星听了，急忙命老妖现了原形，过来谢恩。

[P28] 52 寿星跨鹿要走，悟空一把拉住道：‘老弟别忙，等俺捉到那妖女，一同去到比丘国，交差后才算完事。’寿星只得应允。
53 却说悟空、八戒回到清华洞府，那妖女正想逃跑，悟空一棒下去，打得现了原形。八戒一看道：‘喝！原来是一只白面狐狸。’

[P29] 54 悟空命八戒拖着狐狸先走，自己搬些野蒿荒草，放起火来，把一座妖洞烧了个净光。
55 二人这才约着寿星一同回到比丘国。见了国王，悟空指着白鹿和狐狸道：‘这是你的国丈，那是你的美后！’国王哪敢搭话，只是低头认错。忙吩咐光禄寺安排素宴给圣僧贺功。

[P30] 56 席罢，寿星辞去。唐僧吩咐悟空道：‘妖邪已除，你快去把鹅笼搬回，通报全城百姓认领，好让他们母子早早团圆。’
57 通报传遍全城，人们都迫不及待地涌上街头。鹅笼刚一打开，妈妈上前抱回自己的孩子，亲着、叫着，喜欢得流下泪来。

[P31] 58 全城百姓，情不自禁地抬着唐僧，举起悟空，扛着八戒和沙僧。敲锣打鼓，游街欢呼。家家绘塑影像，户户敬立牌位，永远纪念他们救子的恩情。欲知后事，请看《无底洞》。

full_text_en:
[P1] Biqiu Kingdom
Journey to the West, Chapter Twenty-Nine
Original work by Wu Cheng'en
Adapted by Chen Pingfu
Illustrated by Xuan Yuan Guan Chao
Hebei Fine Arts Publishing House

[P2] Content Summary
This illustrated storybook is adapted from chapters 78-79 of the classical mythological novel "Journey to the West". It depicts Tang Sanzang and his three disciples traveling to the West to obtain Buddhist scriptures, passing through the country of Biqu, where they discover the king is possessed by demons and gravely ill. The foolish king, believing the demons' lies, orders the hearts and livers of over a thousand boys to be used as medicine. He issues an edict, commanding the people to deliver children, who are then placed in goose cages and kept for use. To save the children, Sun Wukong infiltrates the palace, discovers that the "minister" and the king's beloved "beautiful queen" are actually transformed white deer and white-faced fox demons. He then displays his supernatural powers, subdues the white deer, and kills the fox demon. When the two demons reveal their true forms, the king is filled with shame and admits his mistake. The lives of over a thousand children are saved, and the entire city's people are grateful, erecting statues of Tang Sanzang and his disciples to forever commemorate their kindness.
1 On the journey to the West, there is a country called Biqu, ruled by a foolish and tyrannical king. One morning, a Taoist man suddenly arrives, offering his daughter to the king. The king, instantly smitten, immediately selects her to be crowned the beautiful queen, and the Taoist man is also appointed as the minister.

[P3] 2 The king, since having the beautiful queen, indulged day and night, neglecting state affairs. In less than three years, he became pale and emaciated, plagued by countless illnesses. Despite treatment from the Imperial Medical Institute, his condition worsened, and his life was in imminent danger.
3 At this moment, the Minister of State (Guozhang) entered the palace and reported: 'I have a secret remedy from overseas, with all medicines prepared. Only one thousand one hundred and eleven boys' hearts are needed as the medicine's ingredient. If Your Majesty can obtain these hearts, and brew the medicine, you will not only be revived from death, but also live for a thousand years without aging.'

[P4] 4 The tyrant king, upon hearing this, was overjoyed. He immediately issued an edict to select children household by household, ordering them to be placed in goose cages and set before each home for later use.
5 At this time, the four disciples of Tang Sanzang were passing through the city. They saw a goose cage placed before every household and found it very strange.

[P5] 6 Wukong immediately turned into a bee, flew into the goose cage, and saw that inside were all boys aged five or six, some playing, some crying. Wukong found the situation even more suspicious.
7 As the sun set in the west, the four of them arrived at the Jinting Guesthouse (an official lodging) to stay the night. The postmaster (the official in charge of the guesthouse), upon hearing they were monks from the Eastern Tang Dynasty, was especially polite and immediately let them into the best room.

[P6] 8 After dinner, Tang Sanzang asked about the goose cages, which startled the postmaster. He hurried over and whispered, 'Venerable Master, you need not inquire further. Just change your travel permit tomorrow and continue on your journey.'
9 Tang Sanzang felt there must be a reason behind it and held onto the postmaster, determined to get to the bottom of it. The postmaster, helpless, had to send the servants away and told him the whole story about the goose cages, then slipped away after finishing.

[P7] 10 Tang Sanzang, upon hearing this, felt deeply saddened and hurriedly discussed with his three disciples ways to save the lives of the children. Zhu Bajie said, 'Just go to sleep, don't worry about others.' Tang Sanzang scolded, 'You heartless creature! Human lives are at stake—how can we ignore this?'
11 Sha Wujing said, 'Master, do not grieve. Wait until tomorrow when we exchange our travel documents, then we will find out the truth and act accordingly.' Wukong said, 'My brother is right. Master, please rest easy. If that state minister is a demon, I will surely capture him with my golden cudgel. I will never allow him to harm the children.'

[P8] 12 Tang Sanzang thought for a moment and said, 'If we ask about this matter, that tyrant king will not distinguish between near and far, and will treat us all as slanderers and punish us. What should we do?' Wukong whispered, 'Like this, like this...' Tang Sanzang exclaimed, 'Brilliant! Go quickly.'
13 Wukong leaped into the air with a somersault, chanted the true words, and immediately the local City God and Earth God arrived together before him, awaiting his orders.

[P9] 14 Wukong said: 'I beg you all, move the goose cages to the outskirts of the city and keep them safe. Take good care of the children, do not frighten them. After I have eliminated the demons, I will return them to you.' The gods obeyed the order. Suddenly, a fierce wind blew, and all the goose cages vanished.
15 The next day, Tang Sanzang changed into his formal clothes to meet the king. Wukong, still worried, transformed into a tiny insect and perched on his master's hat brim, secretly protecting him.

[P10] 16 The king, upon hearing that the monks were from the Eastern Tang Dynasty on a journey to obtain scriptures, thought to himself: 'Monks who travel from afar must surely possess great spiritual power.' So, he rallied his strength and was helped by attendants to ascend the throne to receive them.
17 After Master Tang paid his respects in the palace and exchanged the travel documents, he had just sat down when the attendant in charge of the audience announced: 'The National Uncle has arrived.'

[P11] 18 After the Minister of State sat down in the golden hall, Tang Sanzang approached to pay his respects, but he was ignored.
19 The Minister of State asked, 'Where do you monks come from?' The King replied, 'We are monks sent from the Eastern Tang Dynasty to the Western Heaven to fetch scriptures, and we are here to exchange our passes.' The Minister of State laughed, 'Monks are always blindly practicing and training. As the saying goes, "Sit, sit, sit, until your buttocks break..."' This made the entire court of civil and military officials burst into laughter.

[P12] 20 Tang Sanzang argued with him for a few moments, but the state minister's arrogance was overwhelming. The king echoed his words, and the officials followed suit, leaving Tang Sanzang utterly discouraged. He then left the golden hall. At that moment, Wukong called out: 'This state minister is a demon. You go back first; I'll stay here to listen for news.'
21 After Tang Sanzang left, Wukong flew into the golden hall and just landed on the jade screen when a guard reported: 'Your Majesty, disaster! Last night, a strange wind swept away all the goose cages in the city, leaving not a trace.' The king was greatly alarmed and stamped his feet repeatedly: 'Without the hearts and livers of children to cure my illness, I cannot survive.'

[P13] 22 The Grand Tutor said to the king: 'If we eat the heart and liver of a monk, it would be even better than a child's.' The foolish king, upon hearing this, turned from worry to joy and complained: 'Why didn't you tell me earlier, Grand Tutor? It would have been better if we hadn't let that monk go.' The Grand Tutor replied: 'What's the difficulty? Just issue an order to surround the inn; even if he flies to heaven, we can catch him!'
23 Wukong heard everything clearly and hurried back to the inn to report to his master. Upon hearing the news, Tang Sanzang was terrified, his eyes wide and mouth agape, and he grabbed Wukong, pleading: 'Dear disciple, save me!' Wukong said: 'If you want to be safe, let the big become small, the master become the disciple, and the disciple become the master. I will go in your place.'

[P14] 24 Change happens instantly. Wukong presses clay onto his own face, makes a mold, sticks it onto his master's face, blows on it, and Tang僧 immediately turns into Wukong.
25 Wukong then switches clothes with his master, shakes his body, and transforms into Tang僧, fooling Bajie and Sha僧 into not recognizing him.

[P15] 26 In an instant, a loud commotion erupted as countless soldiers rushed in. The leading official demanded to see Tang Sanzang. Wukong pretended to bow and said, 'I am the monk.' The official said nothing and dragged Wukong away.
27 Pushing and shoving, they dragged Wukong up to the golden hall. Wukong stood before the steps and shouted loudly, 'King of Bichu, you summoned the monk. Speak quickly!'

[P16] Bring the knife, cut open your chest, if you have a black heart, I will surely send you.
I want your black heart.
28 The King said: "I suffer from a serious illness, all the medicine ingredients are ready, only the medicine引 is missing. If the elder is willing to give me your heart and liver as the medicine引, I will build a temple for you and offer sacrifices four times a year."
Wukong coldly laughed: "I have several hearts, but I don't know what color the King wants?"
29 Wukong cut open his belly, and a pile of hearts rolled out, red, yellow, white... but there was no black one. The officials were frightened, covering their heads and closing their eyes, the King trembled all over like a sieve, shouting: "Quickly take them away, quickly take them away."

[P17] 30 Wukong wiped his face, revealing his true form and said: 'We monks are all full of good intentions, but only you, the State Minister, have a black heart that can serve as medicine. I'll dig it out for you to use.'
31 The State Minister looked and recognized the Great Sage Equaling Heaven from long ago, and immediately turned to flee. Wukong raised his staff to strike, and the State Minister hastily met him with his coiled dragon staff. They fought back and forth for over twenty rounds, with no clear winner.

[P18] 32 Wukong fought with increasing bravery; the National Master was no match for him. Seeing he could no longer defend himself, he feinted a strike and fled, turning into a cold beam of light.
33 Wukong landed from the clouds, arriving at the palace. The entire court of civil and military officials came forward to pay their respects.
Wukong said: 'Don't bow! Go quickly and find your king!'

[P19] 34 Everyone split up to search. They first went to the Beauty Queen's palace, but found nothing. Even the Beauty Queen was gone.
35 In the midst of the chaos, four or five eunuchs were seen carrying the half-dead, unconscious king out from the rear palace.

[P20] 36 The officials rushed forward to greet the king, and in unison they reported: 'Fortunately, a divine monk has arrived, revealing that the Minister of State is a demon. The beautiful queen is not to be found in the palace; perhaps she fled with him.'
37 The king opened his eyes, stared blankly for a while, then leaned on Wukong and asked: 'I saw you once this morning. How come you've changed your appearance now?' Wukong replied: 'I am his disciple Sun Wukong. Because you wanted to eat my master's heart, I transformed into his likeness to come and subdue the demon.'

[P21] 38 The king, upon hearing this, trembled all over, knelt and bowed his head like a garlic clove, begging Wukong for mercy. He then hurriedly adjusted his robes and hat, and ordered the attendants to invite Master Tang to the palace.
39 Master Tang, leading Bajie and Sha Wujing, arrived at the palace steps. Wukong rushed forward, pulled off his master's clay face, changed his clothes, shouted 'Transform!', and behold, Master Tang returned to his original form.

[P22] 40 The king, upon seeing Master Tang arrive, immediately got up from his throne to welcome him, calling him 'Elder Master, Great Buddha,' and helped him up to the hall.
41 After everyone sat down, Wukong asked, 'Where are the king's father-in-law and the beautiful queen from? I'll go get them both and eliminate this lingering threat.' The king blushed deeply and replied, 'When they came, they said they lived at Qinghua Village, seventy miles south of the city, on Liulin Slope.'

[P23] 42 After hearing this, Wukong immediately instructed Sha Wujing to protect the Master well, and together with Zhu Bajie, he rode the clouds and winds to search for Qinghua Village to capture the demon.
43 The two flew seventy li, then stopped their cloud-riding. They saw willows deep in the distance, with a small river running through, stretching endlessly — they couldn't find the village anywhere.

[P24] 44 Wukong chanted a spell to summon the Land God to ask for directions. The Land God said, “There is a Qinghua Cave here, hiding demons. Great Sage, if you wish to find it, go forward from here. When you see the old willow tree with nine branches, turn left three times, then right three times, then strike it hard with your hand, and shout 'Open!' three times. Then the Qinghua Cave will appear.”
45 The two followed the directions and indeed found the old willow tree with nine branches. Wukong ordered Bajie to stand aside and wait for backup, while he himself followed the instructions. With a loud crash, two cave doors flew open, and on the stone screen were written four large characters: “Qinghua Cave Palace.”

[P25] 46 Wukong rushed into the cave and saw the old demon holding a beautiful woman, panting: 'My plan has failed. I was about to eat my son's heart and liver, but that damned Sun Wukong ruined it.'
47 Wukong leaped forward in one swift step and roared: 'Evil demon who harms people, taste my staff!' The old demon was terrified, his soul flying out of his body, and he dropped the woman and fled.

[P26] 48 Pigsy, waiting outside the cave and growing impatient, was about to enter to see what was happening when the old demon suddenly ran out. He swung his rake at the demon, who quickly dodged, flickered his body, and fled eastward in a cold beam of light.
49 The two chased after him tightly, but soon lost sight of the demon. From the clouds emerged the Immortal of the South Pole. Pigsy asked, 'Old man with the meaty head, have you seen the demon?' The demon had shrunk into a ball and hidden behind the Star of Longevity. The Star of Longevity pointed at the demon and said, 'Here, here.'

[P27] 50 Wukong said: 'Old Brother Shouxing, that old demon is causing trouble and harming people, why are you protecting it!' Shouxing bowed and said: 'Great Sage, please calm down. It is my mount — the white deer. It was my carelessness; it stole my cane and ran away to cause trouble. I beg you to spare it!' 
51 After thinking for a moment, Wukong said: 'Fortunately, the children of Biqiu Kingdom were not harmed; otherwise, I would never forgive it!' The old demon trembled with fear. Upon hearing this, Shouxing hurriedly ordered the old demon to reveal its true form and come to express gratitude.

[P28] 52 The Star of Longevity was about to ride his deer away, but Wukong grabbed him and said, 'Brother, wait a moment. Let me catch that demoness first. We'll go together to the Country of Bichu, hand in our report, and then this matter will be settled.' The Star of Longevity could only agree.
53 Then, Wukong and Bajie returned to the Qinghua Cave. The demoness was trying to escape, but Wukong struck her with his staff, forcing her to reveal her true form. Bajie looked and exclaimed, 'Hey! It's a white-faced fox!'

[P29] 54 Wukong ordered Bajie to drag the fox away first, while he himself gathered some wild grass and brushwood, set fire to it, and burned the entire demon cave to the ground.
55 The two then accompanied the Star of Longevity back to the Kingdom of Bichu. Upon seeing the king, Wukong pointed at the white deer and the fox, saying, 'This is your Minister-in-Chief, and that is your Queen!' The king dared not speak, only bowing his head in admission of his mistake. He hurriedly ordered the Ministry of Rites to prepare a vegetarian feast to celebrate the success of the holy monks.

[P30] 56 After the feast, the Star of Longevity took his leave. Tang Sanzang instructed Wukong: 'The demons have been vanquished. Quickly bring back the goose cages, inform all the citizens to claim them, so their mothers and children can be reunited soon.'
57 The news spread throughout the city, and people rushed to the streets in excitement. As soon as the goose cages were opened, mothers rushed forward to embrace their children, kissing and calling out, overjoyed to tears.

[P31] 58 The people of the entire city, unable to contain their joy, carried Tang Sanzang, lifted Wukong, and carried Bajie and Sha Wujing on their shoulders. They beat gongs and drums, parading through the streets in celebration. Every household painted and sculpted their images, and every family erected memorial tablets to forever remember their kindness in rescuing the children. To learn what happens next, please read 'The Bottomless Cave'.

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《比丘国》的封面，标明其为《西游记》之二十九，原著吴承恩，改编陈平夫，绘画轩辕观潮，由河北美术出版社出版。
[P2] 本页为绘本《比丘国》的内容提要和第一幅画面，概述了故事背景：唐僧师徒路过比丘国，发现国王被妖魔所缠，听信妖言要以童男心肝为药引。孙悟空识破妖精，救下孩童。第一幅图描绘了道人献女，国王封其为美后、道人为国丈的情景。
[P3] 本页描绘了比丘国国王因沉迷美后而荒废朝政，身体日渐衰弱，太医院治疗无效。国丈进宫献上秘方，声称需一千一百一十一个男孩心肝作药引，方可让国王起死回生、长生不老。
[P4] 本页描绘了比丘国国王下令按户选送孩童，将其装入鹅笼置于门前；唐僧师徒四人路过此城，发现家家门前有鹅笼，感到十分奇怪。
[P5] 孙悟空化作蜜蜂探查鹅笼，发现里面关着五六岁的小男孩，感到事情蹊跷；唐僧师徒四人傍晚抵达金亭馆驿投宿，驿丞因他们是大唐来的和尚而格外客气，安排他们住进上房。
[P6] 唐僧在金亭馆驿向驿丞打听鹅笼之事，驿丞起初不愿多说，后被唐僧追问，只得将鹅笼的来龙去脉讲了一遍，随即离开。
[P7] 唐僧师徒得知比丘国要杀害孩童后，唐僧心痛不已，与徒弟们商议对策。八戒消极应对，被唐僧责骂；沙僧建议待明日倒换关文时查明真相，孙悟空则发誓若国丈是妖怪，必用金箍棒将其制服，保护孩童性命。
[P8] 唐僧与孙悟空商议如何揭露比丘国杀害孩童的阴谋，孙悟空决定召唤本地城皇和土地神协助。
[P9] 孙悟空请城隍和土地神将城中所有鹅笼移至城外妥善保管，随后唐僧前往皇宫见国王，孙悟空则化作小虫暗中保护师父。
[P10] 唐僧在比丘国皇宫觐见国王，国王强撑病体接见；唐僧刚坐定，当驾官便通报国丈到来。
[P11] 唐僧在金殿觐见国王，国丈傲慢不理；国丈嘲讽唐僧一行是瞎修瞎炼的和尚，引得满朝文武哄堂大笑。
[P12] 唐僧在金殿与国丈争辩无果后离开，孙悟空化作小虫潜入金殿，得知卫兵报告全城鹅笼被怪风卷走，国王惊慌失措，担心无法用小儿心肝治病。
[P13] 国丈向国王提议用和尚的心肝治病，国王大喜并下令围捕唐僧；孙悟空得知后急忙返回馆驿告知师父，唐僧惊恐万分，孙悟空则主动提出替师父前往皇宫。
[P14] 孙悟空用泥模和法术将唐僧变成自己，又与唐僧互换衣物，自己化身为唐僧，使八戒和沙僧无法辨认，为潜入皇宫做准备。
[P15] 孙悟空化身为唐僧被官兵押往金殿，他挺立阶前，高声质问比丘王有何要事。
[P16] 孙悟空化身为唐僧被押入金殿，国王逼其献出黑心作药引，悟空剖开肚皮，滚出各色心肝却无黑心，吓得国王和百官惊慌失措。
[P17] 孙悟空现出真身，揭露国丈黑心，随即与国丈展开激战，双方交手二十多个回合，不分胜负。
[P18] 孙悟空与国丈激战，国丈不敌化光逃走；悟空落地后，满朝文武跪拜，他命令众人去找国王。
[P19] 众人分头寻找失踪的国丈和美后，未果；随后，几名太监搀扶着昏迷不醒的国王从后殿走出。
[P20] 百官向国王禀报国丈是妖邪，美后可能已一同逃走；国王苏醒后见到孙悟空，询问其为何变样，孙悟空解释自己为救师父而化身为唐僧前来降妖。
[P21] 国王被孙悟空揭露真相后惊恐求饶，并传旨请唐僧上殿；唐僧与八戒、沙僧到达后，孙悟空为他恢复原形。
[P22] 国王见到唐僧后恭敬迎接，孙悟空询问国丈和美后的来历，国王称他们来自城南七十里外的柳林坡清华庄。
[P23] 孙悟空吩咐沙僧保护师父后，与猪八戒一同驾云前往清华庄捉妖；飞行七十里后，二人在杨柳深处的小河边降落，却怎么也找不到村庄。
[P24] 孙悟空与猪八戒在土地指引下，找到通往清华洞的九叉头老杨树，按指示拍树呼喊后，洞门开启，现出“清华洞府”石匾。
[P25] 孙悟空闯入清华洞，发现老妖正抱着美女，老妖懊恼计划被破坏；悟空随即上前喝斥并举棒相向，老妖惊恐逃走。
[P26] 猪八戒在洞外等候时，遇到逃出的老妖，举钯攻击，老妖化光逃走；二人追赶时，老妖躲入寿星身后，被寿星指出位置。
[P27] 孙悟空质问寿星为何袒护作怪的老妖，寿星解释老妖是其坐骑白鹿，因偷走拐杖才跑出来作乱；悟空念及比丘国孩童未受害，决定饶恕，寿星遂命老妖现形谢恩。
[P28] 孙悟空阻止寿星离开，要求先捉住妖女再回比丘国交差；随后二人返回清华洞府，孙悟空击打妖女使其现出白面狐狸原形。
[P29] 孙悟空命猪八戒拖着狐狸离开，自己放火烧毁妖洞；随后与寿星一同返回比丘国，当面揭穿国丈和美后的真实身份，国王认错并安排素宴庆功。
[P30] 宴席结束后，寿星离开，唐僧命孙悟空将装有孩童的鹅笼搬回城中，让百姓认领；消息传开后，全城百姓涌上街头，母亲们抱回孩子，激动落泪，母子团圆。
[P31] 比丘国百姓为感谢唐僧师徒救回孩童，抬着他们游街欢呼，家家户户立牌位纪念。页面下方附有《西游记》连环画目录，本册为第31册《连环洞》。
[P32] 本页为《西游记》连环画第31册《连环洞》的版权页，列出了原著作者、改编者、绘者、出版发行信息、印刷信息、书号及定价等出版资料。
